utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A very good afternoon. Please be seated. May we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And today's appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. John Ostojic on behalf of Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And I take it, before we start with the videoconference, that we hear today Mr. Ljuban Jankovic without any protective measures necessary as checked already with Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's start immediately with the videoconference. May I ask for a sign from the audio and video unit, is it fine? Okay. I see confirmed. So let's wait for Charlotte Dahuron to be seen. Yes, she is. First a sound check. Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] I can hear you perfectly. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, everything seems to be fine. So the witness is present. May we have a view throughout the entire room first that we can see who actually is present.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then ask you, Madam Dahuron, to bring the witness in to your room. Good afternoon from The Hague. Mr. Jankovic, can you hear me? Mr. Jankovic, can you hear me? Good afternoon from The Hague. May I start once again. Mr. Jankovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] Could you please retry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jankovic, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] Okay. Not loud enough. We're trying to fix this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. So let's wait a minute. And please tell us when you are ready. So once again, the third attempt: Mr. Jankovic, can you hear us from The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] It's not loud enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Madam Dahuron, can you maybe exchange your earphones or your headphones? Could this solve the problem?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] Okay, let's try again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The fourth attempt: Mr. Jankovic, can you hear us from The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I thank you for coming, testifying in Banja Luka. May we first hear your solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jankovic. You are called as a Defence witness, and therefore, I give now the floor to Defence counsel, Mr. Ostojic. Please, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Jankovic. My name is John Ostojic, and I represent Milomir Stakic. Thank you for appearing and giving your testimony here in this case. Can you hear me, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you please give us your full name, your first and last name, and your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I received no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice on my B/C/S channel, it's almost inaudible also, so the problem may be here with the microphone for the interpreters, not our microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we continue, Mr. Jankovic? Is it better now? Apparently there is a problem in the moment. Mr. Jankovic, one other attempt: Can you hear us here from The Hague in the moment in a language you understand? Mr. Jankovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The translation for Mr. Jankovic is provided here in The Hague or in Banja Luka in this case, Madam Dahuron?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] It's provided in The Hague, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So may I ask the booth, any problems? No, there shouldn't be a problem. Then let's try to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the channel on his microphone is not set for him to receive the B/C/S version if they can just verify that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] We are checking at this moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask somebody from the B/C/S booth to speak a little bit or to read out something that they can test the functioning of the system.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] Your Honour, the witness has confirmed that he can hear well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So everything should be fine now. Mr. Ostojic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Once again, my name is John Ostojic and I am one of the attorneys representing Dr. Milomir Stakic. We would like to thank you for coming and giving your testimony in this case. Sir, once again, can you please give us your full name, first and last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ljuban Jankovic. I was born on the 10th of March, 1953.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, where you were born and in what municipality that was.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in Novi Seher, Maglaj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a little background, sir, relating to your educational experiences. Where did you go to school and what degrees did you obtain?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have completed the school for dentistry in Belgrade, and further on, I specialised in oral surgery, dental surgery in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what year did you complete your medical studies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: 1982 was the year I completed the dental school in Belgrade, and my specialisation, I completed in Zagreb in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you become gainfully employed after you completed your dental specialisation in Zagreb in 1991?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was already employed at the health centre in Prijedor. Therefore, after completing my specialisation training, I returned and started working as a specialist for oral surgery at the health centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us, if you will, the time period in which you were employed at the health centre in Prijedor. From what time to what time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I am employed -- I had been employed since the 2nd of August, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1982, and up until the 1st of February, 1988, was when I stayed working on when I started my specialisation. My specialisation was started at the general hospital in Prijedor, at the department for general surgery, and then starting on the 1st of November 1988, I went to specialisation training in Zagreb where I did my specialisation in oral surgery and facial surgery at the Salata Medical Centre also in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From 1988 through 1992, can you tell us specifically where were you employed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: My official place of employment was the health centre in Prijedor, but starting in 1988, I attended specialisation in Zagreb up until the 4th of March, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us during the period that you were in Zagreb what the atmosphere was like for you as a physician working there up through and including March of 1991.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Simply speaking, they treated me very properly, professionally. I socialised with well-educated people, and there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During the time period, sir, of the spring and summer of 1992, were you employed at the health centre in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe for us what your duties and obligations were in the capacity in which you held during the time period of the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, I was head of dental department at the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive me for asking this question. Can you tell us what your ethnic background is.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if at any time you served in the military.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when, and if more than two occasions, please specify whether you served in the military on more than one or so occasion.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised on the 19th of November, 1991, and I spent two and a half months in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who issued the mobilisation papers which required you to join the military in November of 1991 for two and a half months.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think those were armed forces. That was the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir -- strike that. Tell us in what capacity you were mobilised and where you were mobilised in November of 1991.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I served as a person with medical background, and I was head of the medical corps in the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us during that time period, commencing on November 1991, who was the commander or your commanding officer in the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was either Lieutenant-Colonel or Colonel Pero Colic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, sir, your duties and obligations while being head of this medical unit while you were mobilised with the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: As the head of the medical corps, I had two physicians within my unit, and our tasks were to treat and examine soldiers and civilians that came as patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During your mobilisation, sir, was there any time that you can recall that there was a policy of discrimination against those persons to whom you would be providing medical care as a member of the 5th of Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not. We didn't even know first and last names of the people that came to be treated by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You stated that your tasks were to treat and examine soldiers and civilians that came as patients. Can you describe for us where these people would be coming from and the nature and extent of their injuries, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have in mind soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we treated injured and sick soldiers, and those civilians who lived in the area where we were stationed, the local population, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did at any time, sir, while you were mobilised as -- in the medical corps of the 5th Kozara Brigade, did there come a time ever, sir, that you would have to have contact with the local civilian and municipal political government?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not. I didn't even know a single civilian who was in the organs of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would, sir, and I'm going to ask you, during that time period, would -- were there ever any interference from the civilian local political, municipal organs with respect to the jobs and duties that you were providing in the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Following your mobilisation, can you share with us what you did after the two and a half month period in November of 1991? Did you ultimately leave or were you discharged from the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was demobilised in January of 1992, and I returned back to my professional duties, back to my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And where was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: My job was at the health centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to state that from January through at least April 1992, you continued to work in the health centre in Prijedor? Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During that time period, sir, did you likewise have an opportunity to see the events as they were unfolding in the Prijedor Municipality with respect to any tensions that were on the rise?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, sir, from your perspective, to the best of your recollection, what do you recall about that time period prior to April 1992.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in late March or in early April. I don't go to the stadium area very often. However, I saw many buses, especially carrying women and children, leaving town. I saw them also by the building of the old Jugobanka in April. In April of 1992, several of my colleagues took their annual leave and left the town, never to come back. This is what was going on sometime in late March, early April. What else can I tell you about that time period? For example, a good friend of mine with whom I socialised a lot, an orthodontist, his name was Suljo Mahmuljin and we were family friends, was quite tense and anxious at a certain period of time. And I frequently asked him, Suljo, why are you so tense? And he would say to me, Can't you see the dark clouds gathering over our state? He smoked a lot and he was very nervous, tense. So it seems that nobody slept peacefully at night during that period of time. Those are little details from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive us for asking, but the details may help us get a clearer picture of the events as they unfolded. So with respect to this Dr. Mahmuljin, you mentioned his first name. Was his formal first name Osman, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it was Sulejman.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us or list for us approximately the number and name of other colleagues who left the Prijedor Municipality in late March and early April as a result of the increase in tensions in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. As far as I can remember, there was Dr. Danijel Dzafic who left for Skopje because this is where his wife and children were staying. Dr. Branko Kalember went to Belgrade. Then I think Dr. Smail Hrnic left on the plane from Banja Luka to Belgrade. Then I remember a nurse called Jasna Foric who with her family left Prijedor in a bus. And if I tried hard to remember, perhaps I could come up with some other names. But these are just a few names that I can remember off the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did these physicians and colleagues, as you mentioned, a nurse, did they tell you or share with you the reasons for their departure from the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason given was annual leave, going on a holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I recognise that was the formal reason given to the health centre in Prijedor. But do you know from speaking to them, if you do and if you recall, what did they share with you as to the reasons why they were leaving the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the stories going around, that there was a lot of insecurity felt by people in Prijedor, the need was felt at least to have families move to more peaceful areas in the former Yugoslavia. A lot of people moved to the west. But I think that the reason people were leaving town was the insecurity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, did at any time during these conversations with individuals, did any of your colleagues mention or reference that they were being terminated or discharged from their employment because of their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. We even recorded them as having taken unpaid leave, even though they were absent for more than five days without justification. And the law stated that if somebody was absent for more than five days without justification, they would be terminated. However, we recorded them as being on unpaid leave. And let me give you another example. Our colleague, Danijel Dzafic called us from Skopje and told us that due to certain reasons, he was unable to return to Prijedor. And that was some time in May. We had him recorded as a person on an unpaid leave, meaning that nobody was fired but all of them were considered as having taken unpaid leave. And it was believed that eventually they would return to their workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, during the period from April through September 1992, where were you, whether you were in employed and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was employed at the health centre as head of dental department. I was doing my job, that of an oral surgeon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did there come a period, Doctor, from April through September 1992 that you obtained a work obligation, or did you continue to work in the same capacity as you did prior to April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Which April do you have in mind? The 1st of April or what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, was there a time, sir, that you were issued a work --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did have a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And share with us what period that was.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date. I don't remember. I truly don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I can just suggest, and I apologise for doing so, do you recall it being approximately the spring and summer of 1992? And if you don't remember, please just say so and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I can't remember when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In any event, I believe we've established that during April through September 1992, you were working in the Prijedor Municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, sir, to the extent of your recollection, can you tell us specifically on April 30th, 1992, what events unfolded in the Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of April, there was a takeover, and that is all I can tell you about that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, at the time, prior or after, were you a member of any political party or affiliation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not. I was not a member of any political party, either before or after, only during the period when the League of Communists existed. I was a member, but I left the party in 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, and I'll ask a open-ended question, were you a member of the SDS at any time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, sir, on May 22nd, 1992, we have established essentially that there was an incident at the village of Hambarine. Do you recall or can you share with us if you were involved in treating or caring for any soldiers that were brought to the hospital on or about that date?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that that incident took place on the 22nd of May, and I know that two soldiers were killed. I was not at the hospital at that time. I was in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you later learn, sir, what rank or what unit these soldiers who were killed were members of?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what information or facts you know relating to the attack on the city/town of Prijedor on or about May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any information about that attack. I know that there was an attack on the 30th of May, 1992, but I don't have any other information on that attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, because I'm sure it was an inartful question. Specifically, Doctor, since you worked at the health centre, do you recall whether there were people who were being brought to the health centre to be cared for and treated as a result of the events, namely, the attack on the 30th of May, 1992, in the city/town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. There were persons injured. There were people who asked for medical assistance, both in the health centre and in the general hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, were there any fatalities as a result of the attack on the city/town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. I can't remember the exact number, but there may have been a dozen or two dozen people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me change or switch gears, as we say, to another topic. Did you know of the late Dr. Milan Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you know him professionally, socially, or both?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him professionally because I was a resident in oral surgery at the department of general surgery where the late Kovacevic worked as an anaesthesiologist. So we cooperated as colleagues because I was there for six months at his department.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, and forgive me for doing so, if you know a person by the name of Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know him. I don't know whether you have put that question correctly. I know of him, but I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, my question was if you knew him personally. We'll get to the other issues in a moment. Can you tell us, sir, whether you knew Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us in what capacity you know him, professionally, socially, or in both manners?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I know him professionally, and I can also tell you what period I know him from, if you want me to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it would help facilitate this process.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about Dr. Stakic for the first time during the elections in Prijedor in 1990. I knew that he was the vice-president of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly. I didn't know him personally at that time. But he was well-known all over the town. There were very few people who didn't know -- who knew about our colleague Stakic, so he was not well-known in Prijedor. And I don't know whether he ever worked as a doctor in Prijedor at the time. I absolutely don't know that. I first met him in September 1992. We asked him to see us, to meet with us because we believed that as a colleague of ours, he could be of a lot of assistance about the health insurance fund in Prijedor. We wanted to establish that fund in Prijedor. The alternative was for us to be the branch office of the health insurance fund of Banja Luka, and that was the first time when I actually met Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And since September of 1992, did you have an opportunity to visit and to meet with Dr. Stakic on a number of different occasions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I believe that this was the only meeting that I had with Dr. Stakic. I don't remember when that was, but there was a change of government in Prijedor, and that he was replaced by Kurnoga as the president of the municipality. I don't know when that was, whether it was December or January 1993. And as -- for Dr. Stakic, I don't know where he was at the time. He didn't work at the health centre. Maybe he was mobilised, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time following 1993, did you have an opportunity to see or visit or meet Dr. Stakic again in any capacity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in 1993, I believe it was in May 1993, Dr. Stakic became the deputy of the director of the medical centre of Prijedor, and he was my immediate superior. He was my boss. He was the director of that institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us, sir, for how long you had worked with Dr. Stakic commencing on May of 1993? Did you work for him for a number of months, years?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic remained the deputy of the director of the health centre up to 1995 when the medical centre was split into the general hospital, the health centre, and the pharmacy. In 1995, Dr. Stakic became the director of the health centre, so we had a continuing cooperation from May 1993, when he was the deputy director of the medical centre, up to the year 1995 when he became the director of the health centre. And we cooperated with him, not just me as the head of the dental services, but all of the other heads of different services had to cooperate with Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, when you say "cooperate with Dr. Stakic," you were cooperating and facilitating and ensuring that the patients and the citizens of Prijedor were going to get optimal care and treatment for any illnesses that they may be seeking medical attention. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that sense only, in the sense of the professional discharge of our duties. Nothing else but that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able, sir, at that time, to formulate an opinion based upon a reasonable degree of certainty as to Dr. Stakic's character and integrity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I didn't think too much about Dr. Stakic. My personal opinion, based on the contacts with Dr. Stakic and the way he conducted meetings, the way he treated his colleagues, I can say that he was very quiet, very self-effacing, never raised his voice. It was very easy to cooperate with a man like him. If he had problems, since there are a lot of services in the whole centre, he found the time to talk to the respective head of services and discuss the problems in order to deal with the problems in the most satisfactory way. So it is my opinion that he is a good professional, a good colleague, and that he discharged his duties in a very professional manner. And he discussed with us all of our problems that we had as health-care providers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time during the period that you knew Dr. Stakic, including September of 1992 when you first met his acquaintance, did Dr. Stakic express or exhibit any signs of prejudice or discrimination against Muslims, Croatians, or other non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I am claiming this categorically, no. At all the meetings that we had and that we attended as heads of services, I believe that my colleagues, at least 90 per cent of my colleagues were not politically engaged. They were not members of any of the parties, so we were not in the position, and we did not discuss any other matters but the health care that we were supposed to provide. And that is all we discussed in our jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to go back a little. During the period again April through September 1992, to the best of your recollection, do you remember if a curfew was imposed on the citizens of the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that there was a curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, was that curfew imposed only on Muslim, Croatians, and non-Serbs, or did the curfew apply to you, sir, as a Serb living in the Prijedor Municipality as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The curfew applied across the board, to all the citizens of Prijedor. And that included me as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As a medical professional, again, to the best of your recollection, from April through September 1992, was there, sir, at that time in the Prijedor Municipality a lack of essential supplies such as electricity, water, and medical supplies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There was -- there's no single citizen of Prijedor who will ever forget that period. We didn't have electricity for 40 days. We lacked water, and we had to borrow food from each other. There was a shortage of electricity. All those whose fridges were full of meat and other foodstuff obviously had to either throw it all away or share it with others. So it was a dark period when we went back to medieval ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, during the period that you worked at the health centre, whether it be in 1992 or during the period of 1993 through 1995 when Dr. Stakic was working at the same centre with you, was there at any point that there was a refusal to care for or to treat citizens of Prijedor who were of the Muslim, Croat, or non-Serb ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. There was no question about that, let alone for this to be forbidden for people of other ethnic backgrounds to be treated. That was absolutely not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Dr. Jankovic, on behalf of Dr. Stakic, we thank you, and we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecution, after this surprising early end of the questions put by the Defence, are you prepared for cross-examination immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I am prepared, but I also, if Your Honour wants to take the break, I don't think I have more than an hour at most. Whatever you would like to do, but I'm prepared to start now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think then it's better to proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, first a question: Would I be correct that you -- are you a medical doctor or are you a dentist?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a dentist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You talked about your time in the army during the war in Croatia, that you were mobilised for two and a half months beginning in I believe you said September -- let me check my notes. November 1991. At that time, sir --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time, sir, you were serving in the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army, and the army of Republika Srpska had not yet been formed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You talked then about the influence of civilians, municipal officials on that army, the JNA. At that time that you were serving with the 5th Kozara Brigade, the civilian authorities in Prijedor were headed by Muhamed Cehajic, a Muslim. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So your conclusion about the influence of civilians on the army is based upon your experience in seeing what influence Dr. Cehajic and the civilian authorities in Prijedor had on the JNA fighting in Croatia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I said that. I didn't say that the civilian authorities interfered with the work of the army. There was no influence on the part of the civilian authorities on the army. Absolutely none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. What I am trying to understand is the basis of your experiences to reach that conclusion, your experience is as serving as a medical professional during a conflict outside of Bosnia, in Croatia, with the JNA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, did you take part in any way or serve with the 5th Kozara Brigade during operations in Prijedor such as the attacks on Hambarine and Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with ultimatums given by the Crisis Staff to the people of Hambarine and Kozarac that they would be attacked if they didn't comply with certain demands?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me object to the form of the question, and I think it mischaracterises the prior testimony. And if counsel would like to give the, as he puts it "ultimatums given by the Crisis Staff," then we know from other witnesses, and I won't share it in the presence of the witness, their testimony, witnesses that were brought by the OTP --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, no arguments. No arguments in the moment, in the presence of the witness. Let us hear your response, please, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's necessary, I can -- we can get the documents. But I'm talking about S389. Perhaps it won't be necessary if we simply ask the witness if he heard this. He can answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe it's better to have a breakdown of your question in two parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, did you read Kozarski Vjesnik?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I never. I didn't read it the 1980s, I didn't read it in the 1990s. I don't read it now. I have to tell you one thing, since I have never been a member of any parties and I am not interested in politics, the only thing I am interested in is my profession. I do not read Kozarski Vjesnik. I don't read any other newspapers for that matter except for my own professional papers and trade papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So, sir, just so I understand, your opinions of your knowledge of the relations between the civilian and military authorities in Prijedor in 1992 is based upon your experiences as a medical professional who did not read the local media, was not a member of the government, was not a member of any political party, and was not serving in the army at the time of these events between April and September 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please be more clear. I have not understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Certainly, I'll try to repeat it. I'm sorry. It is a bit of a long question, but it's because I'm trying to summarise several facts. If any of these are incorrect, please let me know. Is it true, sir, that you were a medical professional, you did not read the local media, you were not a member of the army between April and September of 1992, and you were not a member of the government or any political parties during that time period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, just briefly, while you were in Croatia, did you know someone named Cigo Radanovic? Had you heard of him or did you meet him when you were with the 5th Kozara Light Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard of him, but I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, was Cigo Radanovic fighting with a militia, private militia, in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I absolutely don't know that. I've never heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that Cigo Radanovic became somewhat famous at least among the Serbian community in Prijedor for his exploits during the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the man whom I don't know personally and about his fame. Maybe you should ask people who consider him famous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you as a normal citizen of Prijedor. You said you had heard of Mr. Radanovic. Tell us, what did you know about Mr. Radanovic and his role, Cigo, his role in the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about that. What I heard about him was when he was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'll move on to another topic. You said that in September of 1992, you went to see Dr. Stakic because of a concern, you wanted to set up an insurance fund. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I must have asked the wrong question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There's no censorship at all. I just was informed that the link has unfortunately broken down. The trial stays adjourned until 4.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And let's try, whether we are lucky enough, that we have a stable connection, may I ask the audio and video unit immediately to show us Banja Luka. Okay. May I ask you, Mr. Witness, can you hear us once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then please proceed, Mr. Koumjian. Only for the transcript, there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, present since the break is Mette Birkelund, an intern with our office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you talked about having worked directly under Dr. Stakic for some time at the Prijedor health centre. And you talked about his management, that he was a person who would discuss problems. Would you say he was a person who asked those who were working around him if there were any problems and had an open door, you could go and speak to him and he would listen and find out what was going on among those people he was managing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was he an intelligent man, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: He probably is, given that he has completed medical school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When he was the director of the health centre, did the health centre run smoothly given all the problems that you had with resources, et cetera? Did you feel that he was able to control what resources were available?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The health centre doesn't function great today either, and there was no question that it didn't function great in those days. But at least there was effort put in aimed at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you feel that Dr. Stakic had a good understanding of what the problems were that the health centre faced?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know to what extent he was acquainted with it. But in view of the office that he held, he should have been informed about problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was he a person who could make a decision, or was he indecisive?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Ask me specifically about a specific decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to do because I was not present at any of those meetings. But sir, when you went to Dr. Stakic with a request, was he able to give you an answer, either yes or no? Was he the type of person who could give an answer to your request?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Given that he was director, he had authorities that went with that office. And knowing the problems and having had consent, he was in the position to approve something. Well, I can give you a specific example. For example, procurement of medication, he could have, when talking to the head of any department, gynecological, pediatric department, or any other department, he could have a conversation with people from those departments because he was unable to handle it all by himself, and he had to have contact with all the departments and heads of respective departments in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. You mentioned that you went to see Dr. Stakic in 1992 in September in order to, I believe, start an insurance fund. Why is it that you went to see Dr. Stakic who you had not known before that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic was a colleague of ours, and believing that Prijedor should have a health insurance fund, we went to see him, not specifically to request that it be established, but simply to see whether there was a possibility to ensure that Prijedor and its surrounding areas, Dubica, Kostajnica and so on, could have their own fund for health insurance for that area. So there was simply a conversation of a consultative nature to see whether he could give us advice. The other option was to remain a branch office within the Banja Luka health insurance fund.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, I'm sure at that time you knew many other physicians and medical professionals. Would I be correct that the reason you went to see Dr. Stakic, who you did not know personally at that time, was because he was the president of the Municipal Assembly and you thought he could assist you given his position?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It did not cross my mind, but it is possible. I don't know at whose initiative we went there. At the time, there was a medical centre headed by director of the medical centre. The hospital, health centre, pharmacy, and occupational medicine clinic were just units within the medical centre, and there were people heading all of those units. So this question was of interest to all four units within the medical centre. And somebody came up with the initiative to establish health insurance fund because even before all of these events, Prijedor had its own health insurance fund. I don't know whether we went to see the right man. I don't know about that. But we went to see him because we thought he could give us some kind of advice and tell us. I don't know whether it was the Municipal Assembly or the executive council that would eventually have to decide about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You went to the office of the president of the Municipal Assembly, is that correct, in the Municipal Assembly building to have this meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And it was -- Dr. Stakic was the only official present, the rest were the representatives of the medical centre. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So, Doctor, isn't it a fact the reason you went to see Dr. Stakic was because of his position of the president of the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor because you felt he was in the number one position in the civilian government in Prijedor, correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no comment to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, can you just tell us the truth. Is that the reason, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know how relevant my opinion is. I would have to deal with the issues concerning the establishment of the health insurance fund. As I've told you, I'm not interested in politics. I have no political activity. But I don't know to what extent the office of the municipal president, Municipal Assembly president was important. I don't know whether that person is more important or the person heading the Executive Board of the municipality. I don't know. It is possible that we went there just to have a talk, to ask for his advice, to see what further steps should be taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the question has not yet been answered. May I ask the Prosecution to repeat the question because we deserve a correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, isn't it a fact that the reason you went to see Dr. Stakic, a person you did not know before, was because of his position as president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I've said that had Stakic not been a physician, we would have not gone to see him. We went to see him because he was a colleague of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Doctor, how many other colleagues that you had never met before did you go to see to discuss this insurance fund?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not all of the colleagues are qualified to talk about the health insurance fund. There is top echelon of the medical centre, with people who can give a proposal how to establish the fund. We went to Banja Luka to speak to the then-president of the health insurance fund and see whether it should remain in Banja Luka and whether we should be a branch office of it or whether we should have a fund of our own. So it wasn't just Dr. Stakic that we consulted. We also went to Banja Luka about this matter. And I believe that a physician is in the position to discuss this, and not somebody who is not a medical professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, to ask my question again, Doctor, in Prijedor, what other physicians did you speak to about the insurance fund besides Dr. Stakic? Did you meet with all of the physicians in Prijedor, or just with Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: If the five of us met with all the physicians, there would have been perhaps some 60 to 70 physicians attending the meeting altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Instead, you met with only one physician, and that one happened to be the president of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There were many more senior physicians that you could have spoken to such as Dr. Kovacevic, but you didn't speak to Dr. Kovacevic. You went to see Dr. Stakic. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't talk to Dr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And there were many more famous and well-known physicians, such as Dr. Esad Sadikovic. You didn't go and see him about the health insurance fund, did you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Esad Sadikovic was a personal friend of mine. I don't know where Dr. Esad Sadikovic was at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that. Let me move on, and we'll come back perhaps later to discuss your relationship with Dr. Sadikovic. Sir, you talked about some friends of yours or colleagues, excuse me, who had left Prijedor prior to the takeover on the 30th of April. Were there other colleagues of yours that remained in Prijedor who were of non-Serb descent, specifically Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In trying in your own mind to understand why some of your colleagues of Muslim and Croat descent left Prijedor, did you ever consider and do you believe that there was an atmosphere of hostility towards physicians who were Muslim and Croat in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You said that nobody -- you said I believe at one point in your transcript. I can try to find the page. That we had put everyone on unpaid leave. When you say "we," who are you referring to? Were you yourself in charge of placing individuals on leave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not in charge of that personally. There is a service in charge of recording who came to work and who didn't. And what I was saying referred to people who had left for annual leave at the time, who had left the territory of Prijedor and failed to return back to their workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, when you said "we had them on unpaid leave" and I think I can find -- let me try to be fair to you, let me try to read the quote. It's beginning at 14:45:11. You said: "Our colleague, Danijel Dzafic" -- would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. "Called us from Skopje and told us that due to certain reasons, he was unable" --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: From Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. From Belgrade. Okay. And due to certain reasons, he was unable to return to Prijedor. And that was some time in May. We had him recorded as a person on an unpaid leave, meaning that nobody was fired but all of them were considered as having taken unpaid leave." When you said "we," since you yourself were not doing it, did you mean the Serbs working in the hospital, or who did you mean by "we"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, it wasn't just Serbs working there. There were Muslims as well. When I say "we," I mean the service. I don't mean particular people. Had I hadn't myself, I would have said so, or had I meant my colleagues. But when I say "we," I mean the service itself. And as I've told you, during that period of time, there were Muslims employed as well, not just Serbs, at various health-care institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us of any Muslims working in the Prijedor health centre to your knowledge throughout the summer of 1992. Can you give me the names of any who remained throughout 1992, or at least through the end of September. And I'm talking about medical physicians.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you about people from my department. There was Dr. Midhad Besirevic, and also a young doctor who had come from Trebinje. His first name was Mirza. I don't remember his last name. However, they left Prijedor. I don't remember when. They were not fired. They were not terminated. They simply left of their own free will. As for the health centre itself, I don't know about that because I was at the dental department at the time. There were Muslims working, just like Serbs. However, there were some that went of their own will. I've just given you two examples. It wasn't just Muslims leaving. I can tell you that Dr. Goran Papic and his Jadranka also left Prijedor sometime in September. And they are living in Sweden nowadays. They were Serbs and they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I understand that. Let me go back to my question. My question was not dealing with any dentists, but physicians. And I'm not talking about people who left on their own or left for any reason or disappeared in 1992. I'm asking you do you know the names of any Muslim physicians who remained working in Prijedor at the hospital or at the health centre through September 30th of 1992? If you don't know, you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that I have no contact with the hospital. I even did not have contact with the health centre at the time. There was a director of the health centre at the time, and I was heading the dental department. So I am not now referring to the employees of the hospital or the health centre. The dental department in Prijedor is physically separate from the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So I understand your answer to be that you do not know the names of any doctors of Muslim ethnicity working in Prijedor through the 30th of September, 1992. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, in talking about why people leave, were you ever aware of accusations, very threatening -- well, very serious accusations of serious misconduct levelled against people of Croatian, Muslim, or non-Serb descent, such as Dr. Zeljko Sikora or a Dr. Osman Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned a Dr. Mahmuljin, and I believe you said his first name was Sulejman. The Dr. Mahmuljin that you knew, was he a cardiologist?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: He was an orthodontist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That clarifies something. So it would be incorrect that you knew Dr. Osman Mahmuljin, the cardiologist? You did not know him. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, you're incorrect. I did know Dr. Osman Mahmuljin as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm sorry -- thank you for clarifying that. Doctor, I believe there's a document in Banja Luka that I would like to have shown to you, and it is a newspaper article. It has not previously been marked, although the page, Your Honour, was -- Court and counsel have it, of the B/C/S, was previously disclosed. And it's from Kozarski Vjesnik from the 10th of June, 1992. If we can just please be patient with me, sir, because we're distributing copies to people here. Thank you for your patience. The article that I'm going to ask you about is in the upper left. Do you have a copy of that, sir, in front of you now that you can read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be provisionally marked 402A and B respectively.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if it would make sense. I don't have a whole lot more cross-examination, to just have the witness read this article now. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we should proceed as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, could you please read the article, and I would ask you to please read a bit slower than you normally would because it's going to be interpreted. Just pause for a second after each sentence. Please read it out loud now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will, to the extent that I am able to see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Shall I start reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we ask the Registrar, does the witness have the best copy available?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] We have only one copy, and we tried to put it on our ELMO here and maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We don't need it -- whatever is easier for him. We don't need it on the ELMO here. We all have copies.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Banja Luka] [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to put this document on the ELMO, the B/C/S part. And focus on the concrete article, and then be transmitted to Banja Luka from our ELMO. May I ask the witness, can you read the article now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can try. It's not terribly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So that it's clear from the transcript, it's Kozarski Vjesnik of 10 June 1992. Would you please be so kind and assist us in -- by reading out this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I suggest that I read in English, and the interpreters read the B/C/S to the witness as I'm speaking. Would that make sense?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If there are no objections, we can try it this way. So may I ask the witness, if you see a discrepancy or would believe some other words have to be used, then please alert us immediately. The representative of the Prosecution will now read out the document in English, and you will hear it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The top portion of the headline is "Medical treatment of cardiologists Zivko Dukic on the night of the attack of Prijedor. The story. The main headline: "Survived all `therapies.'" "Many of our fellow citizens are sure to remember sentimental soaps such as the hospital at the 'edge of town,' 'the black forest clinic,' or films such as Coma where bribable and corrupt doctors do many evil things and kill their patients. We would all be hard pressed to imagine even the possibility of something like that happening in reality. The recently exposed activities of Dr. Sikora, who had been using deliberately and for years monstrous methods to reduce the birth rate of the Serbian people sheds a completely new light on the professional behaviour" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: "On the professional behaviour of some physicians in Prijedor. Many of us will be taken aback when they hear that certain physicians, too, were treated in, to put it mildly, a strange way. "More than a month ago, Dr. Zivko Dukic, a cardiologist, came down with a serious illness, the very same illness he treated and cured in so many patients during his long working life."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please stop there so the interpreters can catch up with you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: "But on the evening of 28 May, when Dr. Dukic was struck by a coronary failure in his family apartment, not everything was done in accordance with medical ethics. His work colleague, Dr. Osman Mahmuljin, who was on duty that evening at the city hospital coronary unit, thoroughly forgot the words of the Hippocratic oath, thus harming rather than helping the sick Dr. Dukic, namely, immediately upon the arrival of Dr. Dukic, whose freshly done ECG clearly showed an acute infarct, instead of doing what infailingly has to be done in such cases, Dr. Mahmuljin made moves that would surprise even complete medical laymen, let alone the present medical personnel. "There was enough morphine at the coronary unit, but it never reached the sick cardiologist. Oxygen got lost somewhere on its way towards the unit. Things that were the most necessary, that should have been the first for Dr. Mahmuljin to secure for a sick colleague never reached his sick bed. Subsequent therapy received by Dr. Dukic during his two and a half hour long agony is beyond all comprehension. Instead of speeding up his heart rate, Dr. Mahmuljin did exactly the opposite. He decided to administer 2 per cent Zylocaine which further lowers the blood pressure, but administered 800 milligrams of the medication thus exceeding the 750 milligram dose required for a full period of 24 hours. "The frequency of Dr. Dukic's heart sank to almost 40. But Dr. Mahmuljin kept convincing his sick colleague, who was still conscious in spite of his bad condition that the frequency was as high as 60. The agony of Dr. Zivko Dukic lasted from 2100 hours to 2330 hours when Dr. Radojka Elenkov, present director of the Prijedor hospital, arrived at the coronary unit wishing to help her sick colleague. "She is the one who is the most responsible for the fact that Dr. Dukic's heart endured. She discontinued the therapy Dr. Mahmuljin was using on Dr. Dukic, and in the course of the night, new drugs significantly improved the health situation of the sick physician. It is interesting that after his two and a half hour vigil over Dr. Dukic, Dr. Mahmuljin remained in the hospital building for the next two days, although he was not on duty any more and had nothing to do. "The answer to that can be found in the words of Dr. Elenkov, that is the conclusion that impose it is self in this case. 'We know what was going on in our city in these moments and who perhaps should have taken over the power. I may be able to link these things in this sense.'" Doctor, with articles such as the one just read appearing in Kozarski Vjesnik, do you find it surprising that non-Serbs would flee Prijedor in order to preserve their safety and the safety of their families?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Kozarski Vjesnik is the paper that I never -- I've never read. Of course, I'm surprised because I knew Dr. Mahmuljin. He treated my mother who had problems with her heart. And that is all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And your experience, your impression was that Dr. Mahmuljin was an experienced professional cardiologist, and a person who treated everyone, and your mother I presume was of Serb ethnicity, everyone in a professional manner. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your department, was there a Dr. Harambasic, a dentist, working for you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was a lady doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And did this lady doctor, to your knowledge, isn't it correct that she was arrested and taken to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You mentioned other -- that you knew other physicians. Aren't you aware that other physicians were arrested and taken to the camp such as Dr. Ibrahim Beglerbegovic, others were killed in the camp such as Dr. Jusuf Pasic; Dr. Sikora, who was just mentioned in that article; your friend Osman Mahmuljin; Dr. Jusuf Pasic; Dr. Islam Suljanovic; Dr. Enes Begic; and Dr. --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know all of these physicians. Those people worked in the hospital or in the health centre or in Kozarac. I have only spoken about my department, the dentistry department. So I can't tell you what was going on in hospital, who was arrested, who was taken away, because I don't have that information. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Dr. Islam Bahonic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You said you were friends with Dr. Esad Sadikovic. He was a very well-known and popular physician in Prijedor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You were aware that he was --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: He was married to a Serb and had been the head of a peace movement in Prijedor before the conflict. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you're aware he was taken to the camp and has never been seen since he was alive, since he left -- was taken out of the Omarska camp by the police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when he was taken away. But later on, I learned that he was in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Doctor, you said that when Dr. Stakic was the head of the health centre, you attended many meetings with him and that he showed no discrimination towards any ethnic group. Were there any Muslim or Croats present at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That was in the period between 1993 and 1995. I would have to think hard to remember who the heads of the different services were at that time. I don't think that there were any Muslims among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you remember any Croats being at any meetings with Dr. Stakic that you were present at in 1993 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know who Croats were and who were Serbs, because sometimes the family names are the same. So I wouldn't be able to tell you who was of what ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Dr. Stakic speak about your missing colleagues such as Dr. Mahmuljin, Dr. Sikora, Dr. Sadikovic, and discuss what had happened to them? Or did he ever mention their names in your presence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know of anything that Dr. Stakic did to prevent crimes in Prijedor or to punish perpetrators of crimes? If so, can you give us specifically what you know about what Dr. Stakic did.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First question is on your personal background. May I ask you, please, you told us in the beginning of your testimony today that you graduated in Belgrade and Zagreb, and you had vocational training there. May I ask you, did you also have any kind of vocational training in other towns?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever left Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically, are you referring to my period of continuous education? I don't know what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In general for purposes of vocational training, for purposes of holiday or whatsoever, did you ever leave Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: But of course. I attended world international congresses, European congresses, I went to all the professional meetings, seminars. And as for my holidays, I've had holidays in France, in Germany, Italy, not to mention the places in the former Yugoslavia where I had my holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When doing so, did you ever use an airplane?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I have to explain about the airplane. I have a fear of flying. The first time, as the medical student, when I was in the position to go to Spain, I didn't go because I was afraid of flying. To this very day, I have this fear of heights and fear of flying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this is the reason why unfortunately you can't -- we can't have you here in our courtroom which would be even more advantageous --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That is the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you know Professor Cehajic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Another issue: You mentioned that you visited Dr. Stakic in September 1992 in the municipal building in Prijedor. Did you go there spontaneously or did you have an appointment with Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Firstly, I didn't go there by myself. I was a member of the delegation. I didn't go there to see somebody I didn't know at the time. It was my job that took me there, my profession that took me there to meet with Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Who was in your company?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that lady doctor from the hospital, Dr. Elenkov was in the delegation. I believe that Dr. Zec represented the occupational health department. And on behalf of the pharmacy, there was a pharmacist whose name I can't remember. A lady whose name escapes me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, who was the head of this delegation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: There was no particular head of the delegation. Nobody really headed the delegation. Maybe the person who was at the time the head of the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But once again, was there any appointment in advance, or did you go spontaneously to the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that Dr. Elenkov asked for a meeting with Dr. Stakic, so I believe that it was Dr. Elenkov who arranged that meeting. That is what I believe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you recall on which floor it was in the municipal building you met Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you enter Dr. Stakic's office directly or had you to pass another office, another room?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We had to announce our visit with the secretary, who was sitting in a room, and that's where we waited. And then we were shown into his office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did the secretary expect your arrival? Was she aware that you were coming?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I assume that yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the one hand side of this office of the secretary, there was the office of the president of the Municipal Assembly; on the other hand, in the other direction, the office of the vice-president? Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I should have thought so because it was my first visit to that place ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The first, but not the last?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the first time that I went to that particular office. But I did go to the municipal building before, but this particular office, that was the first time when I entered that office. And after that, I never went to see Dr. Stakic in his office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On page 15, line 14, you told us that you knew that he "was the vice-president of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly." When you met Dr. Stakic in September 1992, in which capacity did you meet Dr. Stakic? What was the capacity of Dr. Stakic? Because until now, as mentioned on our transcript, one can only read that you knew Dr. Stakic as the vice-president.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him as the vice-president. I only knew of that fact. The first time I actually met Dr. Stakic was in September 1992. And I absolutely did not know him as a person, as an individual before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have understood this. But let us know, when he was introduced to you, he was introduced to you as the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly or in which other capacity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your testimony would be you spoke with Dr. Stakic not knowing in which capacity he acted in the municipal building at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We came to talk to him as a colleague, as a fellow physician, not as the president of the Municipal Assembly. We would not have come to see the president of the Municipal Assembly if that person at the time had been a civil engineer, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, isn't it true that you knew that at that period of time Dr. Stakic was, in fact, the president of a Crisis Staff? Would it be correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I absolutely don't know anything about Dr. Stakic and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You never heard that there was a Crisis Staff in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard, not of just one Crisis Staff, but of many of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you see Dr. Stakic in uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember ever having seen him wearing civilian clothes either. I absolutely do not remember ever having seen him wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you drive a car in 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Did I drive a car in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You told us now that you knew that Dr. Stakic was vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, and then later that you learned that he was president of the Municipal Assembly. On today's testimony, transcript page 8, line 23, you answered: "I didn't even know a single civilian who was in the organs of authority." Apparently you knew that Dr. Stakic at that time was in the beginning vice-president, later the president. What brings you to the testimony that you "didn't even know a single civilian who was in the organs of authority"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in the organs of authority, in the military authorities. Authorities are usually civilians as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, are you still gainfully employed today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask where?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The same place, the health centre of Prijedor, and I'm still an oral surgeon in the department of dentistry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is today the director of this health centre?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Dr. Spomenka Pavkovic, a pediatrician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What is the role, if any, Dr. Stakic plays today in this health centre?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think he has no role.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When did you see him for the last time in the health centre?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
