utterances.text: When was that? I can't remember the date. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Approximately? You mentioned --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It could have been in 1996 perhaps. Perhaps in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you know whether or not Dr. Stakic is still on the payroll of this health centre?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I believe that he's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One final question: Answering the question put to you by the Prosecution, you mentioned that you were aware that a lady doctor, colleague of yours, was brought to a camp. Did you take the opportunity when being in the Municipal Assembly to discuss this question with Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when was it that the lady doctor was taken to the camp. I learned that through her husband because he personally called me by telephone and told me that she had been taken, not to the camp actually, but that she had been taken -- was it to the police station or some place like that? That's what he told me. And then later on, I learned that she had been taken to the camp. I don't know whether it was six months later or a year later. But at any rate, her husband personally called me and told me that Dr. Biba had been taken to the investigative centre or to the police station. I really don't know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you make any investigations, any attempts to find out where your direct colleague, Dr. Biba, was at that time and what was the reason why she was apparently arrested, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether I was able to do anything because I could yield absolutely no influence. I was not involved in politics, and I really couldn't go to anybody to inquire about anyone. I was simply focussed on my job, and I wasn't interested in other things. The dark -- darkness reigned during those times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But you, as a human being, didn't you have some thoughts why it was that these persons, Dr. Biba and others mentioned by the Prosecution, that they disappeared, what was the reason for this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I really don't know where people disappeared. I don't know whether they stayed in Prijedor area, whether they were taken to camps, whether they were taken to places outside of Prijedor area. That's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But the question would be: Why did they disappear?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I have no answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you think, you as a human being giving me as a human being this answer, I can believe you, that you didn't --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: But let me tell you something. Dr. Biba is in Prijedor nowadays, so she was in the position to leave. She did leave, and today she is back living in Prijedor. So let me tell you something. One had to survive during those times 40 days without electricity, water, no food, illnesses all around. During wartime, people focus on themselves and they care less about other things, especially if they are not interested in politics or other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you take the opportunity to discuss with Dr. Biba when she returned why at that time she was arrested?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I personally have no further questions. Judge Vassylenko?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Judge Argibay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: No questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any additional questions by the Defence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the Court's permission, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, once again, my name is John Ostojic on behalf of the Defence of Dr. Stakic. I want to clarify a couple points if I may, and perhaps you could help me with that. The Prosecution in this case has taken us to a period of certain meetings from 1993 to 1995. And when I asked you the question, sir, on my direct whether Dr. Stakic exhibited any ill will or prejudice towards other ethnic groups, you responded that he did not. The Office of the Prosecution proceeded to ask you who was at the meeting, and you answered that to the best of your recollection, there were no Muslims at the meeting, and you were unsure if there were Croatians at this meeting. My question to you, sir, and I'm giving you this by way of background, my question to you, sir, is the following: Given this opportunity, with all Serbs at these meetings, did Dr. Stakic express in an exclusively Serbian meeting any ill will against other nationalities or any prejudice, or did he promote any ethnic hatred against non-Serbs, given the opportunity that he was simply with his fellow Serbs? Did he share any of those types of views with you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can, but let me clarify something. These meetings starting in 1993 when Dr. Stakic was director were of a professional nature. They were professional meetings of the departments within the health centre. I never heard a discriminating word pass Dr. Stakic's lips during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The meeting in September of 1992, sir, at that time, was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At the meeting of September 1992, sir, when you first met the acquaintance of Dr. Stakic, that also was a meeting which consisted of only Serbs by ethnic background meaning that there were no Muslims or Croatians present when you were trying to obtain assistance for the fund for health insurance. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, sir, during a tragic period in the Prijedor Municipality, did at any time Dr. Stakic with his fellow Serbs express nationalistic views or promote ethnic hatred against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was absolutely no talk of any political matters. Health care was the only topic discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, if I may, and with some leniency with the Court's permission and as well as the OTP's, I understand you didn't read the Kozarski Vjesnik. You were showed an article that we have marked as S402A and B respectively. Is it not true, Doctor, that the reason you didn't read Kozarski Vjesnik was because it was full of such sensationalism and fiction, that which was just read by the OTP to you, and in fact the Kozarski Vjesnik was considered a tabloid newspaper that had a very small and minimal circulation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Not only I do not read Kozarski Vjesnik, but no other paper. As I've told you, I never read them in the 1980s, in the 1990s, or in the year 2000 and on. Those are all tabloids in my opinion. I'm not interested in anything that is outside of the professional realm.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, the Prosecution also asked you questions regarding what Dr. Stakic did to prevent crimes or to punish the perpetrators of the crimes, specifically I believe it's reflected on page 39, lines 20 through 22. My question to you, sir: Are you familiar with the laws that were in place at that time given the situation and the declaration that there was an imminent state of war? Are you familiar with the military doctrine and laws at that time state as to who has the authority, the duty, and obligation to investigate, arrest, charge, prevent, and/or punish perpetrators of a crime? Are you familiar with those laws?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned, sir, a doctor by the name of Dr. Harambasic. Is that the same Dr. Biba that you mentioned, is that the same person, you giving us her first name?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just want to make sure I have the same person. You mentioned she was arrested. Do you know, sir, as you sit here whether she was arrested -- first of all, do you know when she was arrested?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir --

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, who arrested her?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if the civilian political authorities in the municipality ever arrested any individual regardless of their ethnic background in the spring and summer of 1992, or were these arrests, sir, made by either the police, an independent structure, or the military, an independent structure following various provocations and attacks within the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence counsel to refrain from comments and arguments when putting questions to a witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May the witness answer the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not yet. Please, rephrase your question and refrain from these additional comments and arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, let me ask you a question: Do you know whether Dr. Harambasic was arrested at any time after the attack on the Serbian soldiers on May 22nd at Hambarine? Do you know if she was arrested at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The word "arrested," I've heard from her husband that she had been taken in, in to custody for an informative interview. Following the events in Prijedor, that she had been taken into custody for an informative interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir, and I apologise if I misunderstood you. She is still alive, and obviously she would be the best person that we could ask that question of. Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's calling for the witness to give an opinion that he is not qualified --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think under the rules, the Court can take judicial notice of that, but it won't go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, my final question, if I may, the Office of the Prosecution has referenced a person by the name of Cigo Radanovic, and you mentioned a little bit about him, and then I think you mentioned that he ultimately became vice-president of the Prijedor Municipality. Help me and the Court understand, is this Mr. Cigo Radanovic the person who became ultimately the vice-president of the municipality after Dr. Stakic was ousted from the position in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what period of time it was. I know that he was vice-president of municipality, but I don't remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it was at the same time that this Mr. Cigo Radanovic came that other groups replaced members of the Municipal Assembly in Prijedor. Right? Whatever period of time that is; I understand you don't know it, other people were also replaced --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel is leading the witness and suggesting the answers. But I'll stipulate to that fact and Mr. Radanovic was the vice-president when Mr. Kurnoga was president; that's in evidence. We also have a second period which is in evidence according to documents which I could state if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's why if I may reply, it's not misleading. It's in evidence. Similarly, the OTP didn't show documents reflecting when this was. We would like just clarity as to when that was to the extent that the witness knows. Certainly I think by permitting me to ask a couple of questions, we can determine it wasn't before that period because I think the Court has enough information as to who was the president of the municipality prior to that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admittedly, I can't see in the moment the relevance of this at this particular moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Finally, sir, in describing Dr. Stakic when the OTP inquired of him being intelligent, et cetera, did you find Dr. Stakic to be the type of person who had the characteristics or personality that would interfere in the day-to-day activities of a physician at the health centre or clinic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't able to interfere in day-to-day work. He didn't have qualifications for that, nor did he have these -- the scope of authorities. How can somebody who works in a tuberculosis or anti-tuberculosis department work -- or treat patients in a different department? How could he interfere?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When the physicians and medical-care providers would visit Dr. Stakic in 1993, et cetera, they would present problems to Dr. Stakic that they wanted to be taken care of with respect to the health clinic. Correct? Issues that concerned them, whether they would be of a nature of supplies and other matters such as that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, since he was the director, that road had to be taken. The talk with the director was mandatory in order to procure medical supplies, medications, and so on, in order for the department to function properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, Doctor, having worked at that facility, would it have been reasonable for Dr. Stakic to rely on the information that was being given to him in order to assess the situation and make a determination as to what it is that he should do in order to assist?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to. But the meetings were the meetings attended by heads of departments. When a department needed medical supplies, medications, and so on, this was discussed jointly at the meetings in an attempt to find solutions to procure medications or supplies so that the department can function properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you, Doctor. Just one last question: In this meeting in September of 1992 when you met with Dr. Stakic and other colleagues for the fund for the health insurance, was Dr. Stakic attentive and it seemed that he wanted to help in procuring the assistance to the medical professionals that continued to provide to the extent possible cure and treatment to the citizens of Prijedor? Was he helpful during that meeting? He accepted you in the meeting? I'm asking you now: Did he assist in procuring that fund?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that the meeting was very brief, that basic issues concerning the establishment of the fund was stated, and that that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other questions in return by the Prosecution, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So you were able to establish that fund after the meeting in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: The fund was not established. We remained a branch office of the Banja Luka fund. During that period of time, or even perhaps in early 1993, we were a branch office. But it could be that in 1993, later on, the independent fund for Prijedor was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I believe in answer to the last question, the last question of Defence counsel was: "Did he assist in procuring that fund?" Asking about the meeting with Dr. Stakic in September. And your answer was yes. So Dr. Stakic did assist you at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic accepted to meet with us and listened to us carefully concerning the issues regarding the establishment of the fund. However, during that period of time, we were Banja Luka branch office, and the Prijedor fund was established later on. But I don't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Just one other topic. Sir, Dr. Harambasic, this woman, counsel asked if she was arrested after the attack or the incident at Hambarine and whether she was arrested after the attack on Prijedor, the 30th of May. In fact, she was arrested in June of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the attack on Prijedor was on the 30th of May. So the June comes after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Dr. Harambasic was arrested in June of 1992 approximately, the end of June. Is that correct? Does that sound correct to you, in the summertime?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know when she was arrested. I really don't know that. All I know is that after the 30th of May, the month of June comes next. And I don't know when Dr. Harambasic was taken into custody. I know that only because that's what her husband informed me of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And when -- thank you. And when her husband called, he told you that she was originally taken to the Prijedor SUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you subsequently learned that she was taken to the Omarska camp. Correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Doctor, do you have any reason to believe that Dr. Harambasic, this woman, was involved in the incident at Hambarine on the 22nd of May or the attempt to retake Prijedor on the 30th of May? Have you heard anything or do you have any reason to believe that she was involved in either of those events?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear that Dr. Harambasic was involved in anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know of anything, any crime, that Dr. Harambasic committed or was suspected of that would justify her arrest? And detention in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: LJUBAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything at all of her being guilty of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see no further questions. This concludes your testimony, Mr. Jankovic. You are excused. And the videolink is hereby closed. We proceed as usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The line may be disconnected. Let's now turn to the remaining questions. There was a document tendered by the Prosecution today. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just based on relevance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As ruled previously, in order to know what was discussed in the courtroom, this document is admitted into evidence as S402A and B respectively. We have to come back to the document tendered yesterday by the Prosecution under the provisional number S401A. The Defence made the reservation to comment on this today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have S401, and we have examined it. We would like to have the actual original documents from the census which give the information and background of the second individual that appears on S401. Obviously there are some discrepancies with the birth date, specifically the year, and we just would like to know and further inquire as to how -- and I hesitate to say this because I think the Court will deem it as an argument, how the demographic unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, can we go to private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We heard no objections as to the document S401. It is, therefore, admitted into evidence as S401A and, as requested, this was related also to this document as under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, S401.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S401. And we admit into evidence, without any further comments the other documents with the ERN number 02296872 as J30. Let us go into some details of these two documents. This Trial Chamber, to a certain extent, feels misguided by the Prosecution because we believe it would be -- it would have been the obligation of the Prosecution to present these documents before the discussion of Milorad Stakic, whoever this person is. We feel misled, and we feel that we wasted a lot of time on this question based on the line of questions put to witnesses by the Prosecution. I think there is an obligation not only under Rule 68 but when trying to establish a link between the accused and another person, forgot a moment that it was allegedly the brother of Dr. Stakic, when they try to establish such a link, it's the obligation to provide all the material they have in their possession at that point in time. We, in addition, believe that it's a sign of unprofessionalism to have contacted Milorad Stakic the 7th of February, 1991, already, and then not continuing with the necessary. Under Article 29 of our statute, several times the Prosecution has requested the cooperation of Germany and they always got this assistance in criminal matters. And it would be the easiest exercise to ask for the criminal record from the general federal Prosecutor who within 24 hours could have given you the answer about the outcome of the case and where, in fact, based on this file, where this Milorad Stakic was at that point in time, the relevant period as described in the fourth amended indictment. But we regard this information to date as absolutely irrelevant. We are mandated to decide on individual criminal responsibility and not on family-related criminal responsibility. I think the Prosecutor should have known better and not have opened this unfortunate and unhelpful debate opening a side issue with, and by doing so, not leaving the remaining limited power, and this is true, the limited capacity of the Defence, the limited capacity of the Chamber, to the real questions of the case. And these are legal questions. We heard that the Prosecution is not prepared to discuss these legal questions. We have to accept this. And of course, in addition to this, the link, and this is a central point of this case, the link between Dr. Stakic and the crimes. So we deplore this development, but in conclusion we came to the result that it is not necessary to go in any further details of this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I just say one thing even though the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't know who was first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can just -- with respect to J30, and I recognise the Court's comments on page 60, lines 1 through 3, that document is not all that's in the possession of the OTP in connection with this issue. J30's date as generated of last week is just a summary of the material. We would still like to get the entire interview if possible or if the Court deems it appropriate. That would be our only comment in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Anticipating this request, we already decided during the break that we regard this issue as irrelevant for the outcome of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, if I could just briefly address it. First, we agree entirely with the Court that we have an obligation not just under Rule 68 to the Defence, but to the Court not to mislead the Court or to waste time. The issue of Milorad Stakic, while I agree was marginal, it was not irrelevant because -- and it is something that developed during the case. We first came across that name in the documents seized by Mr. O'Donnell which at that time, to be honest, I thought was possibly a pseudonym used by Dr. Stakic. Then, when one of the Defence witnesses testified, we came across documents showing that a Milorad Stakic was working at the Omarska camp. When I said "came across," yes, these documents, all of these documents I'm discussing were in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor I think before we began this case. But there are 3 million pages -- over 3 million pages in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor. We obviously -- none of us knows everything in those 3 million pages. When we learned -- when we requested just about a week ago from the demographic unit to confirm or to provide us that with the information about that Milorad Stakic who -- it does turn out there is a brother of the accused named Milorad, but when we asked for whether there was another, information that would tend to suggest that I believe it was Mr. -- one of the Defence witnesses, I'm not sure he's protected so I won't say his name who worked at the camp who said the person had a different name and was not the brother. When that was confirmed, we immediately turned it over to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber. However, if we had an ill intent to mislead the Trial Chamber or the Defence, it wouldn't make sense for us to immediately when we got that information to turn it over. As for this interview, first, I can't comment upon contacts with governments because many of those are covered under Rule 70. But secondly, the interview raised my suspicions to be honest. It wasn't until we -- because the brother said he had worked at the Omarska camp. It wasn't until the demographic information was obtained that we saw that it does appear that this Milorad working at the camp was someone else, and that's when we immediately turned it over. But all I can ask, Your Honours, is to consider that our intent, my explanation, that our intent was never to mislead the Court and always was, as soon as we found out information that we possibly had been misleading the Court, to immediately turn over the information that contradicted that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification, and I think it was, in fact, helpful. And I think one conclusion of this is that we shouldn't discuss the question of the brother of Dr. Stakic in the future because it has, Dr. Stakic, no relevance for our case. And on behalf of the Chamber, the apologies that we at all discussed this question. And I think it must be -- must have been extremely difficult for you to listen to these discussions and to these unhelpful attempts. But let us now proceed. The question of the relevance has been declared moot. It's not relevant. So the question is now related to the four certified statements. Are there any objections against the admission into evidence of these statements as taken in Banja Luka in the beginning of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just received this this afternoon and looked at them over the last break. And on my quick perusal, they appear to be the same as the documents that we saw unsigned, and assuming that that is true, then we have no objection. I would note that there was one witness who did not fulfill the technical requirements and that he did not have an identification. We believe that is the witness, and we're not asking to insist upon that technical issue in this particular case, so we're not -- we don't object to that 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any comments by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe the witness did have identification, just not a photo ID. But that's acceptable to us. And just for the record, there is one witness who by verification did not sign her name, and I believe the reasons are stated set forth as to why she did not. And we just hope that that's accepted as the signature having had the document read to her specifically. So that there won't be any issues raised in connection with that specific 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecution, can you accept this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Absolutely. I don't see any other alternative. And given those circumstances, that seems appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we also had the chance to go through these documents. The 92 bis statements given by Milan Cuk, by Mira Stakic, by Zorka Cuk, and finally - correct me if I am wrong - what was the first name of Mr. Ratkovic? Nada -- Nadja Ratkovic, are admitted into evidence under Rule 92 bis. For the further proceedings, I learned based on a telephone call with Madam Dahuron that we would receive as soon as certified two additional statements. Then one statement would be based merely on a previous transcript and no additional statement would be taken, only one. And this could be taken in Belgrade Monday next week, but by another presiding officer. And Madam Dahuron is prepared to leave during the weekend and return to The Hague Saturday, Sunday. So one, I was informed, was stricken from the list of maybe 92 bis. May I hear from the Defence which of them it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think the person at issue was Mrs. Divjak, if I'm not mistaken, but I thought that the decision has not been ultimately made to withdraw the statement. If the Court has the information that that was the decision, I will have to accept it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, no, it was only via and not --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I honestly think that there was trouble getting contact with this lady, so because of the deadlines, to the extent that we couldn't obtain that contact, I'm not sure what her personal plans were for this week, that we were going to simply withdraw it if she is not available this week when the Madam Registrar was there. The other two, I believe, the coordinations have been made. There are unfortunately in Belgrade and not in Banja Luka, and that's why there was a little confusion as to where they can sign. They could not travel, from my understanding, travel to Banja Luka from Belgrade because of -- I believe they have children and they are in school and couldn't provide for a caretaker during that trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we expect the remaining two envisaged 92 bis statements by tomorrow, and maybe we then can already decide on these two questions. But only that the parties know, we can only expect the final one beginning or in the middle of next week. In addition, I have to inform the parties that in case there would be no obstacle, unforeseen obstacle, the Chamber witness, (redacted), would be available as of Tuesday next week, only for the purposes of preparation. We don't really know whether he will actually appear, but it is planned. We'll decide later on which concrete date this witness will be heard. Let us first see him being here in The Hague. Anything additional for the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There are just on the 92 bis, if I may, Your Honour. We had originally applied for I believe 16. The Court has granted us 7. And additionally, the Court had granted us one to be provided pursuant to his transcript. Just so that we're clear on the procedure, should we simply file a motion and attaching the transcript in full in our possession, and identifying it as 92 bis, or -- we can coordinate that I'm sure with the Court Registrar and we'll do that. The second question that I have is: Does the Court wish us to present a written request for Mr. McFadden to present the statement? Because we had made that application. I recall the Court granted it. I believe that Mr. McFadden is waiting to get an order from the Court. I have not seen one, and he will not prepare a statement with respect to Dr. Stakic and the time period of his incarceration without an order. But that's my understanding of what's required, and I hope I didn't misstate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The order can be found on the transcript the same date you made the request. And you should identify this order from the transcript maybe with the assistance of our legal officer. As to the question how to present the other documents, please exchange your views mutually. Prosecution, Defence, together with the legal officer. We won't anticipate this because we are in the moment not aware which statement or which part of the transcript it should be. So therefore, first the facts and then the ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't think there's any necessity for such formality. If counsel gives me the transcript or even the date and the witness, we'll look at it, and we can orally agree and just have it admitted, save them from writing one more motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's what we intended since the start of this case, the 16th of April to, avoid unnecessary filings, let's proceed in this way and try to discuss everything orally. We will hear the next witness as scheduled. What do you believe will be the estimate time in real time, may I put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, it is a little difficult having not met the witness. We think for sure with respect to Witness 037 who is appearing via videolink that we should have more than ample time to finish him tomorrow. I think the entire process will take no longer than today's. We think we'll ask him approximately an hour and a half. Again, I hesitate because I'm uncertain. We also have a witness that arrived today at the Court's request who, I believe, although -- I believe his number was 077, if I'm not mistaken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- who I am meeting this evening at 7.30. He will likewise be prepared to proceed immediately after the videolink statement so that we can have a full day tomorrow, unless the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You already anticipated my last question. I would ask you to be prepared that we hear Witness 077 tomorrow. We have a provisionally amended proffer with the caveat that you had had no chance at all. Please be so kind, if there are any additional points of relevance, give us the necessary written hint before we start tomorrow's hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will do that immediately this evening, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There is one other issue that I have to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The Court last Thursday I believe an issue arose with respect to one of our investigators and specifically my conduct in connection with that attempt to procure the investigator to have the right to visit Dr. Stakic, to assist the Defence lawyers in the final stages of this case. I mentioned I believe at that time that I disagree with the categorisation that was attributed to me. I certainly want to apologise to those people who felt that I personally offended them in trying to procure that item. I don't necessarily agree, but I think that's irrelevant. Since that time, the Court was kind enough to check for us what the Detention Unit rules were, and quite candidly, even this morning, we're still trying to find exactly what the interpretation of the rules are. This morning I was told specifically that the rule is clear that only Defence counsel and co-counsel have a right and would be permitted to visit with Dr. Stakic, not anyone with the Defence team, either together or not. We just wanted a clarification on that because we would like this gentleman to assist us, and we think in a joint effort with Dr. Stakic, since he is a lawyer, he would be able to assist us in the four facets left in this case. Namely, the witnesses remaining, we can make informed judgement decision since he has met with some of them as to whether they are going to proceed or withdraw depending on the time constraints; the rebuttal and rejoinder issues that may arise, the oral submissions and ultimately the written submissions. It's important for us to have the cooperation specifically of Dr. Stakic on those issues but as well as the assistance of Mr. Marko Pavic because he has followed the proceedings and has obviously assisted us in bringing the witnesses here. So we again -- we're just uncertain. The Court has given a clear indication of what the detention rules are. I spoke to the Detention Unit himself. I spoke with no less than three people from OLAD. It's still not clear as to whether or not he's approved to visit with Dr. Stakic with our presence and without our presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it was clear enough that the client/counsel privilege is limited to counsel as such, but knowing about your limited capacities, Mr. Christian Rohde was kind enough to discuss this issue with Mr. McFadden in person, and it was granted that additional visits but, of course, monitored visits can take place from now on as far as there is a capacity. But they granted and they stated that there would be no limitation if it remains proportional, put it this way. But there's not the slightest doubt. Please make reference to these decisions taken by Mr. Christian Rohde and Mr. McFadden in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Anything else. This is not the case. I thank everybody for the assistance of today. And this concludes today's hearing. The trial stays adjourned -- let me just interrupt in parenthesis, maybe we can start tomorrow only a little bit later because I have to conduct another initial appearance. But please be prepared to start as scheduled. Therefore, the trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, at quarter past 2.00.
